summary: New idiom: škur mine d-aloho (auch škur m alo) 'Gott sei Dank!'

data.headword: škur mine d-aloho (auch škur m alo) 'Gott sei Dank!'
data.turoyo: N. Škur mine d Ăḷo, ǧule qṭiʕe haw kolawšina.
data.translation: Thank God for it, we don’t wear torn clothes anymore.

rationale: Allowed search finds an incidental example under xlṣ, not an idiom under škr. Repeated independent attestations justify recording the formula here, with verbal/nominal status unresolved.

summary: Infectum thanks can have l-marked or zero-marked persons thanked; 20/2 instead overtly names the kindness u faḏ̣laṯxu. Preserve this complement distinction without changing the inherited sense.
First-person maškanno shows r+n assimilation, while plural maškərina preserves r. Bare, k-/ko- and prospective g- forms can all perform thanks; this alone does not establish a new sense.
The fixed škur formula has m alo or mine/mene d Aloho. The m- frame should not be generalized to all productive thanking constructions until its verbal status is resolved.

The allowed hškr lookup reveals the same Hanna Dewo child discussion with Komhaškrina, while the input gives Komaškrina. This is a source/transcription question, not grounds to collapse both entries or silently insert h.

Is škur in the formula a reduced III Imperativ, a borrowed thanksgiving noun, or an interjection? PrS 29/23 is also labelled 2sg.f by the reader despite the invariant form; no productive feminine paradigm is established.
What is the segmentation and historical government of mine/mene d Aloho compared with m alo?
Collate MAC Hanna Dewo/57 against the hškr 2 I quotation: is h actually present in the recording/transcription, or are both variants used?
